commits.message: unwrap store envelopes in engenty:bridge
commits.body:
The store operations answer with an envelope — { key, value, updated_at }
for a read, { entries: [...] } for a list — and the bridge passed it
through untouched. An App doing `data.get("todos")` received an object
where it expected its array, so `Array.isArray(saved)` was false and the
list silently rendered empty after every reload. Writes worked, which
made it look like persistence was fine until the browser test.

Removing that boilerplate is the whole reason the bridge exists, so the
unwrapping belongs here rather than in every App. The new tests run the
emitted bundle against a fake host and assert what the App actually
receives, instead of matching strings in the output.

commits.message: keep the app-host id inside agentOS's 63-character limit
commits.body:
appHostId() joined two full 32-char normalized UUIDs into
`t-<tenant>-a-<app>`, which is 69 characters. agentOS caps app ids at 63,
so every real tenant/app pair was rejected at deploy time with "appId
must be 1-63 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens" — surfaced to the
agent as an opaque app_build_failed. Short ids in tests and probes passed,
which is why it went unnoticed until an App was created through the UI.

The app half stays whole: it is a UUIDv7 and already unique on its own.
The tenant half is defence in depth and readability, so truncating it to
12 characters costs nothing and brings the id to 49.

app-host's own validator moves from 128 to 63 to match, and now reports
the offending length, so an over-long id fails as a named validation
error instead of inside a build VM.

commits.message: give agentOS a backend entrypoint, or App backends never run
commits.body:
An App ships no package.json, so agentOS's plan resolver saw index.html,
classified the whole deployment as a static site, and never executed the
declared backend. Every app_action — which proxies POST /<action> to the
guest — hit a file server instead.

Verified against agentos-apps 0.2.14 on the dev stack: the old payload
answers POST /collect with 405 "Allow: GET, HEAD"; the same files plus a
synthetic package.json naming the backend as `main` answer 200 from
server.js, and 422 through an imported rules.js.

composeDeployFiles() now injects that package.json whenever the manifest
declares a backend, and propose rejects a declared backend that was never
written rather than shipping a deployment that silently cannot serve it.
An app that ships its own package.json is left alone — the author has
taken over the plan.

Note this changes what the guest serves: with a backend declared, every
request routes to it and static files are no longer served. That is fine
here because the frontend is served from Postgres via /frontend and never
from the guest.

commits.message: bundle multi-file React frontends on the host
commits.body:
App frontends were restricted to one hand-written, self-contained
HTML file. That constraint came from where the frame renders, not
from what agentOS can build — the guest build VM installs with
--omit=optional and fails outright if any .node file survives (Vite's
Rollup ships one), so a real dev-server bundler cannot run there
either way, and the frontend never reaches the app host at all today.

Add a host-side esbuild pass instead: entry.frontend ending in
.tsx/.jsx/.ts/.js switches an App into bundle mode, where multiple
source files, react/react-dom and CSS imports compile into one
document. A curated import allow-list replaces a tenant package.json —
no npm install, no lockfile, no network during build. A new
engenty:bridge virtual module replaces the ~25 lines of postMessage
plumbing every App used to hand-write.

The built document is stored in the new app_versions.frontend_html
column (source stays in `files`, untouched by the build) and is
injected as index.html into the agentOS deploy payload, so bundle-mode
Apps deploy through the exact path single-file Apps already use. The
frame's srcDoc isolation (opaque origin, no cookies, no session) is
unchanged — this only changes how the one document going into it gets
authored.

Verified with a real multi-file React app (components, hooks, CSS
import) rendered and exercised in-browser: submit, state, computed
total, and the imported stylesheet all took effect.

commits.message: time out setup fetches so a hung backend cannot hang login
commits.body:
ensureCurrentWorkspaceUser and requestApiJson issued plain fetch()
calls with no timeout. When a request was sent but never answered — a
dev-server restart, a hung proxy — the promise never settled, and the
SPA's onboarding gate never left "finalizing onboarding" because
nothing raced it.

Add an AbortSignal timeout to both, defaulting to 10-15s. A caller-
supplied signal still wins; only our own default is upgraded from a
raw AbortError so requestApiJson's existing cancellation contract
(bare-abort passthrough for React Query's own cancellation) is
unaffected.

commits.message: add app_config, and enforce the storage manifest flags
commits.body:
Rejects per-app SQLite rather than restoring it. The re-spike showed the
guest cannot reach any actor, and the host-side workaround would move
tenant working data into app-host's Docker volume — breaking the invariant
that Postgres is the source of truth and app-host is a rebuildable runtime.
Export, RLS, tenant-delete cascade and gateway access all exist because the
data is in Postgres. SQL inside an App buys nothing we have scoped.

What was actually missing was an axis, not an engine. app_data is keyed by
session_id, so an App could not remember anything between artifact
instances — no user preference, no tenant default. module_apps.app_config
is that axis: same narrow key/value API, no session_id, with a tenant-wide
default level and a per-user level that shadows it.

Uniqueness is two partial indexes rather than one constraint, because
Postgres treats NULLs as distinct and a single unique over a nullable
user_id would admit duplicate defaults. setConfig is update-then-insert for
the same reason: ON CONFLICT cannot name a partial index through PostgREST.

The proxy stamps user_id from the authenticated caller, exactly as it
already does for session_id, so an App can only ever reach its own user's
level — it cannot write the default everyone else sees.

Also closes a gap found on the way: storage.data was declared in the
manifest and checked nowhere. A flag nothing enforces is decoration, and
shipping a second one next to it would have doubled the lie. Both are now
enforced by the proxy, and an undeclared store returns 403 before core is
asked.

commits.message: re-spike SQLite against the Rivet cookbooks
commits.body:
The cookbooks work and ours did not, so the question was which of the two
was wrong. Neither: running the cookbook's exact rivetkit/db pattern in
our own process against our own registry passes first try.

The difference the cookbooks never have to draw is who defines the actor.
Every Rivet example is one trusted process owning its own actors, which
works. An engenty App is untrusted tenant code in an agentOS guest VM,
and the only route from there to an actor is the loopback bridge that
returns an empty socket handle. The blocker was never SQLite — the guest
cannot reach any actor at all, and SQLite was just the first thing that
needed to.

Records the implication: a host-defined per-app storage actor keyed
[tenantId, appId] would reach real SQLite through the existing engenty
data_* bridge, which does not touch the broken path. Not implemented;
app_data still ships.

commits.message: harden the engenty Apps runtime
commits.body:
Phase 7 of PLAN-engenty-apps.md, plus two corrections to the plan where it
claimed protection that did not exist.

The kill switch was the first. The plan said "apps.enabled off" was one; it
is not. No module in this repo reads a feature flag in an operation handler,
and PluginServerApi has no request-time resolver to do it with — the flag
gates settings visibility and nothing else. So the real deployment switch is
ENGENTY_APPS_ENABLED=false, which works by not registering the operations at
all: with it off there is no surface to reach. It is opt-out, not opt-in,
because a silently inert module is worse than either. Per-tenant gating stays
module licensing; per-app stays app_archive.

Resource ceilings were the second. agentOS Apps exposes replica scaling but no
per-app memory or CPU knob, so the container boundary is the only real lever:
mem_limit 3g, cpus 2.0, pids_limit 4096 on engenty-app-host, and maxReplicas
lowered from the package default of 128 to 32. That is weaker than per-app
limits and the plan now says so rather than implying otherwise. Same for
egress: the frame CSP genuinely enforces deny-by-default for an App's
frontend, but agentOS exposes no per-release network permission, so a
backend's outbound access is whatever the sidecar allows. Treat it as
unbounded until upstream exposes it.

Also recorded what remains deliberately open: many app VMs share one sidecar
process, which is adequate for buggy AI-generated code inside one tenant and
not for a tenant actively attacking the host — one sidecar container per
tenant is the answer, and it is a deployment change rather than a rewrite.
And capability handles are in-process, which caps apps/ai at one replica while
Apps are in use.

DEPLOY.md gains an operations section: the two native child processes, the
durable volume whose loss takes every App offline, and the token both services
must be restarted together to rotate.

41 module tests.

commits.message: make Apps usable by copilot and coordinator
commits.body:
Phase 6 of PLAN-engenty-apps.md. The plan predicted this needed no
agent-assembly changes, and that held: the operations are ordinary catalog
entries reachable through engenty_tool_execute, and module skills are surfaced
to agents at runtime through the module-skill hint and skill_search, so
neither engenty.copilot's nor engenty.coordinator's manifest is touched.

Two skills carry the patterns:

- app-usage (interactive): check what the tenant already has before building
  anything, open an App as an artifact so the user can find it again, and know
  that a high-risk action pausing for approval is correct behaviour to explain
  rather than a failure to retry. Also says plainly when NOT to reach for an
  App.
- app-batch (headless): do the deterministic work, leave the result in a
  session the user can open, and comment what was prepared BEFORE pausing —
  so whoever approves sees the result, not just the request. Includes the
  standing suggestion to approve recurring actions "for this routine", and
  instructs the agent to report an App whose rules live only in its page
  script, because a batch cannot enforce policy it cannot import.

The consumption tests assert the claim instead of restating it: the discovery
operations really are low-risk and un-gated, app_call_privileged really does
carry requiresApproval, and the skills really are seeded with the owning
module stamped in.

38 module tests.

commits.message: add engenty.coder — the agent that authors engenty Apps
commits.body:
Phase 5 of PLAN-engenty-apps.md. No git, no repo checkout, no external
harness: authoring an App is writing a handful of files and letting the build
be the arbiter. Version A's GitHub machinery is not needed here.

The doctrine is where the work is. Three rules carry most of the weight:

- Declare the least. The manifest is what a human reads before saying yes, so
  ask for the two operations you use, not the ten you might.
- Mark risk honestly. Marking a money-spending action low to dodge the
  approval prompt is called out as the single worst thing the agent can do.
- Rules live in a pure exported function — no DOM, no fetch, no clock — so the
  browser and the monthly batch import the same implementation. If rules only
  ran in the browser, batch runs could not enforce policy and a second,
  divergent implementation would appear, which is how expense systems rot.

The agent has catalog reach and no tenant credentials: it writes code that
asks for what it needs, and a human holding apps.approve decides. It cannot
approve, activate, roll back or archive its own work.

The engenty-bridge skill documents the failure the runtime will not spell out:
an approval-pending result is not an error and must not be retried in a loop.

Note for whoever lands feat/coder: that branch defines a different agent under
the same id, engenty.coder, for repo work. defineModuleAi throws on duplicate
ids, so one of the two needs renaming before both are on main.

32 module tests.

  approval prompt is called out as the single worst thing the agent can do.
- Rules live in a pure exported function — no DOM, no fetch, no clock — so the
  browser and the monthly batch import the same implementation. If rules only
  ran in the browser, batch runs could not enforce policy and a second,
  divergent implementation would appear, which is how expense systems rot.

The agent has catalog reach and no tenant credentials: it writes code that
asks for what it needs, and a human holding apps.approve decides. It cannot
approve, activate, roll back or archive its own work.

The engenty-bridge skill documents the failure the runtime will not spell out:
an approval-pending result is not an error and must not be retried in a loop.

Note for whoever lands feat/coder: that branch defines a different agent under
the same id, engenty.coder, for repo work. defineModuleAi throws on duplicate
ids, so one of the two needs renaming before both are on main.

commits.message: add the engenty Apps capability wall in apps/ai
commits.body:
Phase 4 of PLAN-engenty-apps.md. POST /ai/apps/:appId/call is the single
route every App call passes through, in three directions that share no
credential:

- frontend → app backend: the browser's own JWT authenticates here; the proxy
  reaches the app host server-to-server and the browser never learns its
  address.
- frontend or agent → engenty: the requested operation is intersected with the
  App's manifest allow-list and then invoked with the CALLER's own token. An
  undeclared operation is 403 before core is ever asked. This is what "the app
  connects using the user's auth" means concretely — the user's identity, the
  app's declared subset, enforced server-side, never delegated.
- app backend → engenty: an opaque capability handle, never a token.

Deliberately NOT inherited from /ai/mcp-apps/call: that route authorizes at
server-URL granularity, so a widget may call any tool on any server registered
to the tenant. Here the unit of authorization is the individual operation id.

On handles (app-capabilities.ts): actor tokens were never an option. The
actor-token route mints a token carrying the target user's ENTIRE grant set,
and nothing server-side restricts a caller to a declared set of operation ids
— every mechanism named "grant" widens rather than restricts. So a backend
gets 32 random bytes that mean nothing outside this process, resolve to
(user token, app, allowed operations), expire in five minutes, and are minted
and revoked per invocation. They are explicitly not JWTs: verifyAccessToken
accepts any HS256 token carrying tenant_id + sub as an ordinary session token,
so a signed handle would be a full session credential by accident. A handle
also only ever narrows — presenting one cannot reach past the subset it
carries, even if the manifest allows more.

v1 keeps the handle registry in-process. That is a trade, not an oversight:
resolving from Postgres would require apps/ai to hold a service credential on
exactly the path that must never have one. A restart or a second replica fails
closed. module_apps.app_capability is where this moves for multi-replica.

Action routing preserves the approval story: a manifest action marked
high-risk goes to app_call_privileged, so a headless coordinator run pauses
into the durable approval flow instead of slipping past it. Data operations
are scoped to the proxy's session id, not to whatever the guest claims, so an
App cannot read another session's working data by asking for it.

23 new tests; 616 apps/ai tests pass.

commits.message: render engenty Apps in the artifact pane via a bridged frame
commits.body:
Phase 3 of PLAN-engenty-apps.md — the piece that makes Apps visible.

The MCP Apps host frame already existed but was reachable only from the chat
transcript, and the pane's html renderer ran scripts with no bridge at all. So
the transport half of McpAppFrame is lifted into BridgedFrame and two very
different guests now share one audited bridge: MCP widgets in the transcript
(tools/call → a registered MCP server) and engenty Apps in the pane
(tools/call → the app proxy under a manifest allow-list). What is deliberately
NOT parameterised is the isolation — srcdoc without allow-same-origin, so the
guest has an opaque origin, no cookies and no reachable platform session.

New artifact type `app`, whose content is a {app_id, session_id} handle rather
than the app itself. The frame is keyed on the immutable release, not on the
artifact content string, so a session_id change or a no-op version bump does
not tear down a running frame and destroy what the user was mid-way through.
The listener binds once per frame via refs; an inline callTool arrow from the
parent would otherwise re-bind it every render and drop in-flight replies.

No show_app tool was needed. An App instance IS an artifact, so the existing
show_artifact opens one with zero new machinery.

Also added: ui/notifications/message so a frame can say something into the
conversation — text only, capped, because the guest is untrusted and gets to
speak, not to render. And a size-changed guard: in pane mode the host owns its
height and a guest cannot resize it.

CSP tests lock the deny-by-default shape: widening connect-src for a declared
host must not widen default-src or frame-src, and the policy meta must land
before any guest markup.

655 ai-ui tests pass; apps/ai artifact tests unaffected.

commits.message: add modules/engenty-apps — apps, versions, governance, catalog ops
commits.body:
Phase 2 of PLAN-engenty-apps.md. Postgres is the source of truth for an App;
the app host is only a runtime, so losing all of its actor state means
redeploying from app_versions.files rather than losing an app.

Schema module_apps: apps, app_versions (unique (app_id, version) as the
concurrency gate), app_capability, app_consent, app_data. Every table has RLS
and explicit service_role grants — a baseline that creates tables without them
produces "permission denied for schema" at runtime and has broken a release
here before. app_capability and app_consent get RLS with no policies on
purpose: deny-all is right for a credential table.

app_data stands in for the per-app SQLite the plan wanted. That path is
unavailable upstream (SPIKE-agentos-apps.md §4), so the app-facing API is
deliberately a narrow get/set/delete/list over (session_id, key) and the
backing store can become SQLite later without changing a single App.

Two decisions worth their comments:

- app_call vs app_call_privileged. A gateway operation declares risk
  statically, but an App's actions vary. So low-risk actions ride app_call
  (no approval) and anything the manifest marks high-risk or
  approval-requiring rides app_call_privileged, whose contract carries
  requiresApproval — which means a headless coordinator run pauses into the
  durable approval flow with no new machinery. Each operation refuses the
  other's actions, so neither can be used to launder the other.
- app_data_* is un-gated. It touches the App's own scratch store and never
  tenant business data; prompting for every keystroke of app state would
  train people to click approve.

Release activation is gated on a new apps.approve capability rather than on
tenant admin, so a department lead can sign off on their own app without
holding "*". It needs no registration — the capability catalogue is derived
from operation contracts — and tenant.member holds module.* rather than "*",
so members do not inherit it. Building happens before approval on purpose: a
human should not be asked to sign off on a release that does not compile.

26 tests covering the release state machine (build failure keeps the same
draft and attaches the log, a rejected proposal never takes a live app
offline, exactly one version stays active, rollback rebuilds from stored
source) and the call allow-list. PRO-only and closed-source per the
2026-07-25 decisions.

commits.message: add apps/app-host — runtime for tenant-authored engenty Apps
commits.body:
Phase 1 of PLAN-engenty-apps.md. An internal Hono service wrapping
@rivet-dev/agentos-apps: deploy source into an agentOS VM, issue requests
into it, tombstone it. Verified end to end against the real runtime — a
backend app deploys in ~22s into its own Rivet namespace, request bodies
and the opaque capability header reach the guest intact, and state
accumulates across requests.

Security posture: the service publishes no port, is not a gateway target,
and takes no Traefik labels. It runs tenant code, so it deliberately has
no origin of its own — serving it on the platform origin would make tenant
HTML same-origin with the SPA and able to read the Supabase session out of
localStorage. Internal calls are gated on a shared secret and the process
refuses to boot in production without one. App ids are validated against a
url-safe pattern at the edge, so traversal is a 400 rather than a
downstream failure.

Ships patches/@rivet-dev__agentos-apps@0.2.14.patch. Without it deployApp()
cannot succeed at all on any published version — see SPIKE-agentos-apps.md
§2. The Dockerfile asserts the patch survived install, and that both native
child binaries (rivet-engine, agentos-sidecar) are present and executable,
so a mis-architected image fails at build rather than at first deploy.

Build failures return 422 with the verbatim build log rather than an opaque
500: agentOS raises them inside the app actor, so they arrive re-hydrated as
plain RivetErrors and instanceof does not hold. Classifying by contract is
what gives engenty.coder something to iterate against — a bad source file
now comes back as 'workspace/index.js:1:33: ERROR: Expected "}"'.

24 tests. Typecheck, build, env-example sync and the test-wiring guard pass.

commits.message: add engenty Apps plan + Phase 0 agentOS spike findings
commits.body:
Phase 0 gate result: @rivet-dev/agentos-apps is self-contained (RivetKit
auto-spawns a native Rivet Engine plus an agentOS sidecar; no Rivet Cloud,
no token), but two independent defects in the published preview:

- guest processes cannot write through createHostDirBackend, so the release
  tar step fails and deployApp() never succeeds on 0.2.13 or 0.2.14 — the
  package's own README example does not deploy. A ~15-line patch that packs
  into the guest VFS and reads the artifact out with the host-side AgentOs
  API fixes it; static and backend apps then deploy and serve.
- the guest network bridge returns an empty socket handle for the scoped
  Engine proxy, so the RivetKit-in-guest path (the only route to per-app
  SQLite) 500s on every request. Not patchable from our side.

Decisions recorded in the plan: ship the patch and build all seven phases;
module_apps.app_data is the v1 app store in place of SQLite; PRO-only;
a new apps.approve capability gates release activation; egress deny-all;
modules/engenty-apps is closed-source for now.

commits.message:
fix(deploy): survive the edge cold build — raise DTS heap, drop concurrency

v0.1.69's edge image build OOM'd: a cold full-workspace build (edge now also
builds the Manage portal) exhausted the tsc worker heap that tsup --dts spawns
(ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY on @engenty/projects). Production was untouched — the
image only pushes on success and the deploy job was skipped.

- ENV NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 in the edge build stage so the DTS
  worker has headroom
- per-service build concurrency: edge (the heaviest image) drops to 2, the rest
  stay at 4, so the concurrent DTS workers fit the runner's RAM

commits.message:
fix(ui): gate the entire /setup surface to superadmins

The Setup nav group is already superadmin-only, but several /setup/* route
guards were looser than the nav — reachable by direct URL:
- /setup/plugins rendered for any admin (tenant admin included)
- /setup/roles allowed isSuperAdmin || isTenantAdmin
- plugin-contributed /setup/* (e.g. /setup/connectors) defaulted to isAdmin

Setup is the install-owner (platform) surface; tenant config lives under
/settings/*. Require isSuperAdmin for every /setup/* route, and make setup
paths superadmin-only regardless of a contribution's requiresAdmin. Tenant
admins keep their /settings/* surfaces unchanged.

commits.message:
feat(tasks): make agent task runs durable and consistent

Seven fixes converging the task/agent runtime on one model, where the
task row is the authoritative record rather than a side effect of
whatever apps/ai happened to write.

- Dispatch and checkout agree on which statuses are pickable (todo,
  backlog), so a task can no longer be dispatched into a state its own
  checkout refuses.
- Stale checkouts are reaped: a run that dies without releasing no
  longer parks its task in_progress forever.
- Goal handoff to the coordinator is a coordination TASK, not a
  bespoke pgmq queue plus consumer — both are deleted. Handoff now
  travels the same path as every other piece of agent work.
- Approval re-runs are honest: an approved operation re-dispatches
  through the normal run, instead of reporting success for work that
  never re-executed.
- Thread ids are deterministic per task run, so a resumed or retried
  run reattaches to its own conversation.
- Run outcomes are durable on task_runs (finished_at, outcome). The
  previous best-effort write to ai.agent_run left failed writes
  showing "in progress" indefinitely.
- Pending approvals live on the task (pending_approval_operation_ids),
  not on a dismissible inbox notification. Dismissing the message no
  longer strands the task with no route back.

Adds an hourly coordinator heartbeat routine with a schedule-stacking
guard, and fixes ROUTINE.md bodies never reaching the agent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(manage): recover to login on an expired/invalid session

When the stored JWT referenced a GoTrue session that no longer exists (e.g.
after a core restart), the workspace-context query 401'd and the app showed a
dead-end 'Authentifizierung erforderlich' card with no way back to login.

Now a 401 / session-gone error from the context query triggers a local
signOut(); onAuthStateChange flips isAuthenticated -> false so the login screen
renders. Non-auth (transient) errors still show the retry card. Verified live by
tampering the stored token: the page auto-recovers to the login form and a fresh
sign-in returns to the console.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Adds the first Observability section to the manage console:

- Logs: date/file picker, level filter, server-side search and paging over
  /api/logs/files + /api/logs/entries (superadmin, evlog jsonl + agents stream).
- Audit: cross-tenant security-event feed. The existing

  other, so this adds superadmin /api/superadmin/audit/{events,distincts}
  that allow an optional tenant_id (omitted = every tenant). The adapter
  already returns all tenants when tenant_id is absent; only the route gate
  needed relaxing. Tenant/type/module/actor/search filters + paging; rows
  expand to the raw detail JSON.

STICKY_HEADER_CLASS, PageShell/PageState) and are wired into a new
"Observability" nav section. en/de locales + vitest specs included.

of `isLoading`, so a paused/reconnecting fetch (no data, no error yet) shows
loading rather than the "could not load" dead-end card. Source dir is
`pages/log-inspector` because the root .gitignore excludes any `logs/`.

  legitimate cross-tenant platform-console view, mirroring the audit routes
  (requireSuperAdmin, records an approval.decided audit event w/ viaSuperadmin).

non-superadmin 403); existing same-tenant decide flow still green.

commits.message:
feat(ai): governance seam for self-managed vs centrally-managed AI settings

Abstract AI model settings + usage limits so the open-source build ships
tenant self-service while a managed platform governs them centrally from the
manage app, without forking the UI.

Enforcement hardening:
- Preflight checkUsageLimits on the streaming chat run path (429 on block);
  previously only the non-streaming generate() path enforced.
- Enforce allowed_models at model resolution (resolvePurposeModel demotes an
  out-of-list tenant/session pin to platform/default) and in the gateway
  model-options picker.
- Admin gate on PATCH /ai/registry/agents/:id.

Governance seam:
- ai.tenant_usage_policy.managed_by ('tenant' | 'entitlement') column + a 409
  lock on the tenant-facing PATCH /ai/v1/usage/policy (superadmin bypasses).
- Entitlement apply path stamps managed_by='entitlement' for packaged tenants,
  'tenant' when un-packaged (removing a plan reverts to self-service).
- Limits tab renders read-only with a "Managed by your plan" banner when
  governed; models tab stays editable within the plan allow-list with a note.
- Manage app: AI governance panel on TenantEntitlementsTab (allow-list + AI
  hard limit + enforcement) written through the entitlement override.

Also moves the AI settings page /setup/ai -> /settings/ai (it edits tenant
config, so it belongs under Settings, not Setup), with redirects + nav move.

Concept + decisions: docs/wip/ai-governance.md.

commits.message:
chore(publish): keep the closed surface out of the open mirror

The snapshot publisher (run by CI on every release tag) had drifted from
publish-open.sh: packages/entitlements was closed there and absent here, so the
next tag would have pushed it to the public repo. Close that gap and add the
gaps this branch would have opened:

- exclude packages/entitlements and the manage-only dev helper
- move the manage/tenancy/entitlements/AI-governance design docs from docs/wip
  (published) to docs/internal (excluded)
- run the dev stack with --filter=./apps/* instead of naming apps/manage:
  turbo hard-errors on a filter pointing at a missing directory, so the open
  repo could not run `pnpm dev` at all
- add scripts/publish-open-exclusions.test.ts, which fails when the two exclude
  lists drift and when a new open->closed workspace dependency appears

That last check documents two pre-existing violations: apps/ai depends on
@engenty/engenty-remote and apps/core on @engenty/entitlements, both filtered
out of the mirror — so `pnpm install` on the public repo currently fails.

commits.message: governance seam for self-managed vs centrally-managed AI settings
commits.body:
Abstract AI model settings + usage limits so the open-source build ships
tenant self-service while a managed platform governs them centrally from the
manage app, without forking the UI.

Enforcement hardening:
- Preflight checkUsageLimits on the streaming chat run path (429 on block);
  previously only the non-streaming generate() path enforced.
- Enforce allowed_models at model resolution (resolvePurposeModel demotes an
  out-of-list tenant/session pin to platform/default) and in the gateway
  model-options picker.
- Admin gate on PATCH /ai/registry/agents/:id.

Governance seam:
- ai.tenant_usage_policy.managed_by ('tenant' | 'entitlement') column + a 409
  lock on the tenant-facing PATCH /ai/v1/usage/policy (superadmin bypasses).
- Entitlement apply path stamps managed_by='entitlement' for packaged tenants,
  'tenant' when un-packaged (removing a plan reverts to self-service).
- Limits tab renders read-only with a "Managed by your plan" banner when
  governed; models tab stays editable within the plan allow-list with a note.
- Manage app: AI governance panel on TenantEntitlementsTab (allow-list + AI
  hard limit + enforcement) written through the entitlement override.

Also moves the AI settings page /setup/ai -> /settings/ai (it edits tenant
config, so it belongs under Settings, not Setup), with redirects + nav move.

Concept + decisions: docs/wip/ai-governance.md.

commits.message: tenant-scope the approval queue, add superadmin cross-tenant routes
commits.body:
The pending-approval queue is a process-global in-memory map, but
/api/security/approvals + /:id/decision were gated by `requireAuth` only and
returned/decided EVERY tenant's requests — any authenticated user in any tenant
could list and decide all tenants' pending approvals.

- Scope /api/security/approvals to the caller's tenant (list filters by
  tenantId; decision 404s a request that isn't the caller's, so a foreign id
  isn't even revealed).
- Add superadmin-gated /api/superadmin/approvals + /:id/decision for the
  legitimate cross-tenant platform-console view, mirroring the audit routes
  (requireSuperAdmin, records an approval.decided audit event w/ viaSuperadmin).
- Manage's approvals page now calls the superadmin routes.

3 new superadmin route tests (cross-tenant list, cross-tenant decide,
non-superadmin 403); existing same-tenant decide flow still green.

commits.message: P4a observability — logs inspector + cross-tenant audit
commits.body:
Adds the first Observability section to the manage console:

- Logs: date/file picker, level filter, server-side search and paging over
  /api/logs/files + /api/logs/entries (superadmin, evlog jsonl + agents stream).
- Audit: cross-tenant security-event feed. The existing
  /api/security/audit/events pins to the caller's own tenant and 403s any
  other, so this adds superadmin /api/superadmin/audit/{events,distincts}
  that allow an optional tenant_id (omitted = every tenant). The adapter
  already returns all tenants when tenant_id is absent; only the route gate
  needed relaxing. Tenant/type/module/actor/search filters + paging; rows
  expand to the raw detail JSON.

Both pages use the shared design system (AdminListTableView, Table,
STICKY_HEADER_CLASS, PageShell/PageState) and are wired into a new

commits.message: recover to login on an expired/invalid session
commits.body:
When the stored JWT referenced a GoTrue session that no longer exists (e.g.
after a core restart), the workspace-context query 401'd and the app showed a
dead-end 'Authentifizierung erforderlich' card with no way back to login.

Now a 401 / session-gone error from the context query triggers a local
signOut(); onAuthStateChange flips isAuthenticated -> false so the login screen
renders. Non-auth (transient) errors still show the retry card. Verified live by
tampering the stored token: the page auto-recovers to the login form and a fresh
sign-in returns to the console.

commits.message: make agent task runs durable and consistent
commits.body:
Seven fixes converging the task/agent runtime on one model, where the
task row is the authoritative record rather than a side effect of
whatever apps/ai happened to write.

- Dispatch and checkout agree on which statuses are pickable (todo,
  backlog), so a task can no longer be dispatched into a state its own
  checkout refuses.
- Stale checkouts are reaped: a run that dies without releasing no
  longer parks its task in_progress forever.
- Goal handoff to the coordinator is a coordination TASK, not a
  bespoke pgmq queue plus consumer — both are deleted. Handoff now
  travels the same path as every other piece of agent work.

Seven fixes converging the task/agent runtime on one model, where the
task row is the authoritative record rather than a side effect of
whatever apps/ai happened to write.

  backlog), so a task can no longer be dispatched into a state its own
  checkout refuses.
- Stale checkouts are reaped: a run that dies without releasing no
  longer parks its task in_progress forever.

  bespoke pgmq queue plus consumer — both are deleted. Handoff now
  travels the same path as every other piece of agent work.

  through the normal run, instead of reporting success for work that
  never re-executed.

  run reattaches to its own conversation.

  previous best-effort write to ai.agent_run left failed writes
  showing "in progress" indefinitely.

  not on a dismissible inbox notification. Dismissing the message no
  longer strands the task with no route back.

commits.message:
feat(tasks): durable tool approvals for routine/task runs + routine linkage

When a headless task-job run hits a tool that requires approval, it now ends
gracefully and surfaces a needs-input inbox notification + task comment instead
of silently deferring to core. The task parks at `blocked` until a human
approves — from the inbox, the task, or the routine — with scopes Allow once /
Allow for this task / Allow for this routine. Approval writes a durable grant
and re-dispatches the task, which passes the pre-gate on the next run.

- New AI approval policy "request": the task-job specialist pre-gates against
  the effective grant set (task ∪ once ∪ routine) and reports ungranted ops via
  an onApprovalRequired callback; the workflow records the durable artifacts.
- tasks.trigger_id links a task back to the routine that created it; shown as a
  "Routine" row in the task sidebar. tasks.approval_grants(+_once) and
  triggers.approval_grants store the allow-lists (pre-configurable on a routine).
- New gateway op tasks_resolve_tool_approval + POST /api/tasks/:id/tool-approvals;
  tasks_clear_once_approvals consumes one-shot grants at brief time.
- Inbox inline actions, task pending-approval card, routine "Approved tools"
  editor, en/de locales.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(core): stop startApiServer boot test flaking on CI's 90s timeout

~77s locally (suite import cost is 40-86s), which intermittently crossed the
90s budget on CI's contended runner (2 workers + apps/ai running alongside).
Not a hang: measured 76.8s locally, and the sibling boot test right after runs
in ~1.2s once the modules are warm. Raise the budget to 180s and retry once —
the retry re-runs in the same worker with plugins already imported, so a slow
cold first attempt no longer fails the suite.

commits.message:
fix(memory): doc-editor dirty false-positives, handle-inside-card, aligned record cards

Three usability fixes on /settings/memory reported from live testing:

- No spurious "unsaved / changed underneath" on mere navigation. onChange
  marked the doc dirty on ANY editor emission, but TipTap emits an update just
  from loading/normalizing the snapshot on mount (and on the live-refresh
  remount) — so opening a tab immediately showed the amber banner. Dirty now
  tracks a real semantic diff against the loaded snapshot (the same comparison
  the save already uses).

- Keep the +/drag block handle INSIDE the white card. The editor's default rail
  sits outside the content edge (left: -3.375rem), which spilled out of the
  bordered card and wasted space / collided with the nav on a narrow main area.
  Scope `.memory-doc-editor` to drop the gutter into a reserved left rail
  (content pl-14) so every block shares one left edge.

- Restore the record cards. memory-doc.css wrapped already-resolved theme
  colors in hsl(var(--card)) etc., but this app's tokens are full oklch /
  color-mix values, so those declarations were invalid and the border/
  background/chip color silently dropped — making the block padding read as
  random indentation. Use the vars directly (matching the tiptap styles).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(tasks): task dependency graph — blocked_by_task_ids + auto-wake (coordination Phase 1)

Expresses "A is blocked by B" as a first-class set so dependents auto-dispatch
when blockers resolve and independent branches run in parallel — parallel
fan-out falls out of the graph, no concurrent sub-agent primitive needed.

- Migration: blocked_by_task_ids uuid[] on module_tasks.tasks + GIN index.
- domain/task-blockers.ts (pure + injectable): openBlockerIds (only 'done'
  resolves; cancelled stays open), validateBlockedBy (self-block, unknown id,
  and transitive-cycle rejection; replace-not-merge).
- api/task-dispatch-service.ts: dispatchTaskIfReady gates enqueue on open
  blockers (flips to 'blocked', no dispatch); wakeBlockedDependents unblocks
  (blocked->todo) + dispatches dependents whose last blocker just hit 'done',
  and comments on a parent once all children are terminal.
- Wired into every dispatch site (tasks_create/update gateway ops, REST
  create/patch, trigger-fire) + wake-on-done in the update handlers.
- DAL: persist the column; getBlockedByIds/loadTaskStatuses/listDependents/
  listChildren/recordActivity.
- coordinator-workflow skill: Blocked audit category + wire-real-dependencies
  guidance (never serialize independent work).
- Tests: task-blockers (7) + task-dispatch-service (9) — diamond graph,
  cancelled-stays-open, cycle rejection, unblock+dispatch, parent completion.

commits.message:
feat(ai): per-agent iteration cap (limits.max_steps) governance dial

Converts the global-only ENGENTY_AI_AGENT_MAX_STEPS iteration cap into a
per-agent setting: an agent's config can tighten its own reasoning-iteration
budget, layered over the global default and clamped to the hard ceiling (60).

- ai-core: agentLimitsConfigSchema + `limits` on agentConfigSchema (exported
  from index + browser). Persisted-shape can grow (budget, etc.) without
  further schema churn.
- resolveAgentMaxSteps(override?) prefers a finite per-agent value, else the
  env default; ceiling always enforced (per-agent can only tighten).
- session-service resolves the cap per-run from the agent's config
  (agentConfig.limits.max_steps) instead of a service-level constant.
- registry-store: map/persist the `limits` jsonb column (mirrors guardrails).
- core migration: ai.engenty_ai_agents.limits jsonb default '{}'.
- Tests: max-steps resolver (7) — override precedence, ceiling/floor clamp,
  non-finite fallback.

Note: per-agent cumulative BUDGET caps (cost/tokens) are intentionally NOT
added here — usage metering aggregates only by tenant+user, so per-agent
budgets need a metering change first (documented follow-up), and dead knobs
are worse than none.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: task dependency graph — blocked_by_task_ids + auto-wake (coordination Phase 1)
commits.body:
Expresses "A is blocked by B" as a first-class set so dependents auto-dispatch
when blockers resolve and independent branches run in parallel — parallel
fan-out falls out of the graph, no concurrent sub-agent primitive needed.

- Migration: blocked_by_task_ids uuid[] on module_tasks.tasks + GIN index.
- domain/task-blockers.ts (pure + injectable): openBlockerIds (only 'done'
  resolves; cancelled stays open), validateBlockedBy (self-block, unknown id,
  and transitive-cycle rejection; replace-not-merge).
- api/task-dispatch-service.ts: dispatchTaskIfReady gates enqueue on open
  blockers (flips to 'blocked', no dispatch); wakeBlockedDependents unblocks
  (blocked->todo) + dispatches dependents whose last blocker just hit 'done',
  and comments on a parent once all children are terminal.
- Wired into every dispatch site (tasks_create/update gateway ops, REST
  create/patch, trigger-fire) + wake-on-done in the update handlers.
- DAL: persist the column; getBlockedByIds/loadTaskStatuses/listDependents/
  listChildren/recordActivity.
- coordinator-workflow skill: Blocked audit category + wire-real-dependencies
  guidance (never serialize independent work).
- Tests: task-blockers (7) + task-dispatch-service (9) — diamond graph,
  cancelled-stays-open, cycle rejection, unblock+dispatch, parent completion.

commits.message:
feat(ai): agent_propose — governed agent-registry writer for the coordinator

The dynamic-agent runtime (DatabaseProvider + assemble-dynamic-agent) existed
with no writer. This adds the writer path, with memory-module-style
governance: agents propose, humans approve, nothing an agent writes goes
live on its own.

- migration: ai.engenty_ai_agents gains status
  ('proposed'|'active'|'archived', default active), proposed_config (pending
  revision for an ACTIVE agent so it stays online while evolving), and
  created_by_agent provenance
- store: runtime reads (getAgentConfig/listAgents) filter to active;
  proposeAgent / approveAgent / rejectAgent + listAgentRecords governance
  view; human upsertAgent stays direct-to-active and supersedes pending
  proposals
- routes: POST /registry/agents/:id/propose|approve|reject +
  GET /registry/agent-records; approve provisions the core.agents principal
- tool: agent_propose (builtin registry) — proposes new specialists or
  revisions, stamps the proposing agent, notifies approvers via inbox;
  approve/reject are deliberately NOT tool-exposed
- coordinator: agent_propose in agent.json + "Growing the team" mandate
  rules in AGENTS.md (propose sparingly, minimal capabilities, mandates
  not prompts)
- tests: store governance contract (6), tool contract (3), chainable-eq fix
  in the guardrails fake

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(platform-settings): platform-wide settings, tenant credential overrides & connection agent

Adds a DB-backed settings store so platform keys/credentials can be set from the
UI (superadmin Setup), overridden per tenant, and resolved with env as the
permanent fallback — plus an in-chat connection agent that guides users to
connect integrations.

- packages/platform-settings: encrypted store (AES-256-GCM via secrets-sdk,
  AAD-bound, KeyWrapper for the KMS phase), DAL, resolver (tenant → platform →
  env → default), consumer + boot-hydration helpers.
- core.platform_settings migration: single table, both scopes, value_enc for
  secrets, service-role only, not realtime-published.
- Env manifest gains a `configurable` flag + a bootstrap-secret denylist; API
  routes (superadmin platform + tenant overrides), secrets are write-only.
- Setup UI (/setup/platform) + tenant Integration keys (/settings/integration-keys).
- Consumers honor overrides: connector OAuth clients resolve tenant→platform→env
  across connect/exchange/refresh; a connections `configured` flag drives a
  "Needs setup" affordance; AI/ingest/bot keys via boot-time env hydration.
- Connection agent: connections_request_connect op + in-chat connect card.
- Docs: setup/platform-settings.md + connections OAuth section.

test: prove memory reflection loop earns its keep (round-trip + wiring)

Adds the end-to-end coverage the memory loop was missing:

A) modules/memory/src/reflection-roundtrip.test.ts — drives the real
   memory_record_upsert gateway handler and the real retrieval source
   (buildDocument/hydrate) against one shared in-memory row store, proving
   a reflection-written record (source_kind 'reflection') becomes indexable
   and hydrates back on the next task — no model, no Supabase. Also pins the
   governance/recall interlock: an org-scope agent write lands 'proposed' and
   stays out of recall until a human approves it.

B) Extract runReflectStep() from reflectStep with injectable ReflectionDeps
   (behavior-preserving) so a test can assert the step delegates a reflection
   run with ONLY the memory tools, deny policy, the task's own agent, the task
   run id in its own thread — and stays fail-open when the run throws.

A) modules/memory/src/reflection-roundtrip.test.ts — drives the real
   memory_record_upsert gateway handler and the real retrieval source
   (buildDocument/hydrate) against one shared in-memory row store, proving
   a reflection-written record (source_kind 'reflection') becomes indexable
   and hydrates back on the next task — no model, no Supabase. Also pins the
   governance/recall interlock: an org-scope agent write lands 'proposed' and
   stays out of recall until a human approves it.

B) Extract runReflectStep() from reflectStep with injectable ReflectionDeps
   (behavior-preserving) so a test can assert the step delegates a reflection
   run with ONLY the memory tools, deny policy, the task's own agent, the task
   run id in its own thread — and stays fail-open when the run throws.

commits.message: platform-wide settings, tenant credential overrides & connection agent
commits.body:
Adds a DB-backed settings store so platform keys/credentials can be set from the
UI (superadmin Setup), overridden per tenant, and resolved with env as the
permanent fallback — plus an in-chat connection agent that guides users to
connect integrations.

- packages/platform-settings: encrypted store (AES-256-GCM via secrets-sdk,
  AAD-bound, KeyWrapper for the KMS phase), DAL, resolver (tenant → platform →
  env → default), consumer + boot-hydration helpers.
- core.platform_settings migration: single table, both scopes, value_enc for
  secrets, service-role only, not realtime-published.
- Env manifest gains a `configurable` flag + a bootstrap-secret denylist; API
  routes (superadmin platform + tenant overrides), secrets are write-only.
- Setup UI (/setup/platform) + tenant Integration keys (/settings/integration-keys).
- Consumers honor overrides: connector OAuth clients resolve tenant→platform→env
  across connect/exchange/refresh; a connections `configured` flag drives a
  "Needs setup" affordance; AI/ingest/bot keys via boot-time env hydration.
- Connection agent: connections_request_connect op + in-chat connect card.
- Docs: setup/platform-settings.md + connections OAuth section.

commits.message:
fix(memory): declare UI in manifest so apps/ui dep survives sync (CI lockfile guard)

The memory module's UI plugin is detected two different ways: the catalog
generator uses the ui/plugin.ts convention (so @engenty/memory needs to be an
apps/ui workspace dep to resolve the dynamic import — memory is a leaf module,
not transitively hoisted), while scripts/lib/engenty-modules.mjs moduleHasUi
keys off the manifest's ui.entry. Without a ui field the deps-sync
(pnpm engenty setup) considered memory a non-UI module and stripped
@engenty/memory from apps/ui/package.json, leaving pnpm-lock.yaml drifted —
which failed CI's frozen-lockfile verify step.

Declare ui.entry (+ ui.route.module.memory in provides, mirroring the other
UI modules) so moduleHasUi is true and the sync keeps the dep. Runtime is
unaffected — the core loader already resolved the same UI entry by convention.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(engenty-remote): resolve migration timestamp collision blocking all migrations

Two migrations shared version 20260720100000: the core ai_push_subscriptions
migration (already applied everywhere) and engenty-remote's grants follow-up.
supabase migration up applies ai_push_subscriptions first, records version
20260720100000, then aborts on the remote-grants file with 'duplicate key
value violates unique constraint schema_migrations_pkey' — blocking every
migration after it, locally and in the deploy migrate container (which is why
prod has been 503 since v0.1.49, unrelated to the memory release).

Rename the never-applied remote-grants migration to a free later timestamp
(20260720100001). ai_push_subscriptions keeps 20260720100000 (must not move —
it is already recorded). Verified: pnpm db:migrate now applies remote_grants,
module_memory, and module_memory_updated_by cleanly and reports up to date.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(remote): grant service_role on module_remote + surface settings errors

Two defects found while testing the settings UI:

1. The baseline module_remote migration created the schema + tables with RLS
   but never granted the service_role usage/CRUD, so the module DAL (service
   client via PostgREST) failed with 'permission denied for schema
   module_remote' — the binding upsert (and every op) was broken in any
   deployment. Add the grants every other module already has. (PostgREST must
   also list module_remote in its exposed schemas — the standard per-schema
   step; the CREATE SCHEMA already drives [api].schemas on local setup, and
   cloud Supabase needs the one-time exposed-schemas update.)

2. The settings page swallowed op failures (no onError), so the create/update/
   delete/revoke mutations and the list queries failed silently. Add sonner
   toast.error feedback on all four mutations and on list-load errors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

New `engenty modules add <package>[@version]` command for a deployed/consumer
instance: installs the module from the registry (pnpm add -w), registers it in
engenty.plugins as { source: registry } (with a package override when the name
diverges from @engenty/<slug>), regenerates artifacts (engenty setup), and
optionally applies migrations (--db-migrate). The prod PostgREST exposed-schema
step is printed as a deliberate next step, never fired at a remote DB from here.

awaits a real consumer install; smoke-verified the CLI registers + renders.

commits.message:
feat(modules): publish modules to GitHub Packages as overlays (Level A / A5)

Publish workspace modules to GitHub Packages (@engenty scope) on release tags —
the 'modules as overlays' model (Option B): a published module installs on top
of a running platform that already provides the internal @engenty/* packages.

- scripts/publish-modules.mjs: a pure, tested manifest transform (strip private,
  stamp the release version, move @engenty/* deps -> peerDependencies as
  host-provided, keep third-party deps, drop devDeps, pin publishConfig) applied
  to a STAGED copy — the committed package.json is never mutated, so local dev
  keeps its workspace deps. npm publish per module; --dry-run stages + packs.
- .github/workflows/publish-packages.yml: release-tag trigger, GITHUB_TOKEN
  packages:write auth. Safe by default — dry-runs unless the repo variable
  PUBLISH_PACKAGES_ENABLED == 'true' (mirrors COOLIFY_DEPLOY_ENABLED), so
  landing this never publishes until deliberately enabled.
- No root .npmrc: a repo-level @engenty:registry mapping would make the
  monorepo's own install hit the registry; the scope mapping belongs in the
  consumer's env only (documented).
- docs/content/dev/module-packaging.md: the A1/A3/A5 story + publish/consume.

Validated: transform unit test (6) + full dry-run across all 28 modules (each
staged as @engenty/<slug>@0.1.45, deps/peers split correct), source untouched.
First real publish is a deliberate step: land + set PUBLISH_PACKAGES_ENABLED.

commits.message:
fix(ci): stop the ai/edge deploy build OOMing (concurrency + reliable cache)

The build-images ai/edge jobs failed/hung repeatedly on v0.1.45: the Dockerfile
default TURBO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY=10 builds @engenty/ai + all 28 modules with
tsup --dts (1-2 GB per worker) and OOMs the runner — @engenty/projects#build
died with ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY. CI already caps this at 4 on the same
runner class; the image build never got the override (DEPLOY.md documents 4 for
constrained hosts). Pin TURBO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY=4 via build-arg.

Also harden the build step:
- registry-backed layer cache (GHCR) instead of type=gha — the 10 GB GHA cache
  cap + export stalls were behind the earlier build-push hang; no cap on GHCR.
- 45-min per-step timeout so a genuine stall fails ~15min before the job cap
  instead of hanging the full hour.

Remote turbo cache wiring (TURBO_API/TURBO_TOKEN into the Docker build) lands
with the cache server.

commits.message:
feat(modules): load registry-installed modules from node_modules (Level A / A3)

Compose the app from modules installed via the registry (node_modules), not
just workspace modules/ — the 'install a module' half of Level A.

New plugin source "registry" in engenty.plugins: resolveEnabledModules (both
the runtime @engenty/environment twin and the build-script twin) resolves such
a module's dir to node_modules/<packageName> (default @engenty/<slug>,
overridable via .package for names like @engenty/pdf-templates-module).
Everything else funnels through that single seam:

- UI catalog + Tailwind (plugin-artifact-generator): the convention resolvers
  now accept node_modules roots, so a registry module is cataloged (imported
  via its package export) and its ui/ source is registered as a Tailwind
  @source — the source ships in the tarball (A1), which is what makes the
  Tailwind scan work.
- Migrations (aggregate-module-migrations): registry modules contribute
  owners from node_modules; the workspace scan now excludes registry slugs so
  a lingering modules/<slug> checkout can't duplicate them.
- Runtime discovery (core loader): registry modules are appended as package
  candidates and load exactly like workspace modules (server + AI face are
  jiti-loaded from the package source). A registry module shadows any leftover
  workspace candidate of the same slug.

Verified end-to-end against a packed tasks tarball extracted into node_modules:
catalog + Tailwind @source point at node_modules, migrations aggregate, config
check passes, environment/core/ui suites green (+4 new registry-resolution
tests). Browser-level Tailwind confirmation (a real UI build) is the one
follow-up. publishConfig/registry wiring is A5 (GitHub Packages @engenty).

commits.message:
feat(modules): package each module as a self-contained tarball (Level A / A1)

Add a per-module .npmignore so every module under modules/ is pnpm pack-able
and complete. Verified across all 27 module packages: pack is clean (no
tests/dev/__tests__/.turbo) and complete (server entry src/plugin.ts, ai/
assets where the manifest declares capabilities.ai, supabase/migrations where
migrationsDir is set).

Key finding driving the blacklist-not-whitelist choice: the platform loads a
module's server + AI face from SOURCE via jiti at runtime, including in prod
(manifest.ts resolves ./src/plugin.ts, loader.ts jiti()s it; defineModuleAi
scans ai/agents + ai/skills by path relative to the registrar's runtime
location). AI assets (agent.json, SKILL.md) are never emitted to dist/, so a
build-only or files-whitelist package would silently drop the AI face and
per-module root files (e.g. tasks/task-status-builtins.ts). dist/ still ships
(UI app consumes ./ui/plugin via the package export).

publishConfig/registry is deferred to A5 (no registry convention established
yet). See PLAN-module-packaging.md Phase A1.

feat(notifications): make the email notifier source-agnostic

The unread-after-delay email channel was hard-scoped to team-chat
(`source = 'team-chat'`). Generalize it to any per-user inbox record via
an operator allowlist `ENGENTY_EMAIL_NOTIFICATION_SOURCES` (comma-separated;
`*` = all sources; default `team-chat` so existing installs are unchanged).
Any producer calling `emitInboxNotification({ source, ... })` — agents,
tasks, heartbeats — can be opted in without code.

Env names generalized to `ENGENTY_EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED` /
`ENGENTY_EMAIL_NOTIFICATION_DELAY_MINUTES`, with the old `…_TEAM_CHAT_…`
names honored as a fallback. Email copy neutralized (source-neutral body).

commits.message:
feat(memory): org governance + skill self-authoring (Phase 4)

Org proposals:
- proposal creation (org-scope agent write → status='proposed') enqueues a
  memory_approval dispatch; new apps/ai consumer writes a high-priority
  tenant-inbox notification (same queue contract style as team-chat)
- audit events via the module audit seam: memory.record.proposed /
  approved / archived
- approved org memories injected into task briefs (highest-confidence
  first, capped at 8) alongside project learnings; the interactive copilot
  reaches them through an explicit org-recall rule in the memory
  instructions (no per-turn DB read in instruction assembly)
- reject path = human archive of the proposed record (approvers only;
  agents remain blocked from touching proposals)

Skill self-authoring:
- skill_propose tool (copilot + CLI agent): drafts SKILL.md into a new
  proposed/ area under ai/skills/ — a sibling of managed/custom that
  skill discovery deliberately does not walk, so proposals are invisible
  to skill_search until approved; approver notified via inbox
- routes: GET /ai/skills/proposals, POST /ai/skills/proposals/:name/
  {approve,reject} — approve copies into the custom tier (discoverable)
  and removes the proposal; managed tier stays read-only (409 guard kept)
- note: repo has no skills admin UI to extend; enable/reject ships as the
  HTTP surface + inbox deep-link (memory approval UI lands with Phase 6)

feat(memory): memory document UI — TipTap doc projection + diff-sync (Phase 6)

Each scope reads and edits as ONE continuous document (/settings/memory)
while module_memory.records stays the source of truth:

- projection: projectRecordsToDoc (kind sections, slug-stable order,
  archived out) + diffMemoryDoc (create/update/archive ops; round-trip
  law property-tested: unedited projection ⇒ zero ops)
- memoryRecord TipTap node: isolating block (heading + body), identity on
  node attrs, provenance chip via CSS data attributes (no NodeView),
  amber styling for proposed blocks, renderMarkdown so whole-doc
  serialization keeps block content
- optimistic concurrency: upsert carries expected_updated_at; stale token
  throws memory_record_conflict (verified live: conflict → toast +
  reload-merge in the page); human edits keep the record's original
  source_kind and stamp the new updated_by column (small migration)
- /settings/memory: Profile (Mastra working-memory viewer, reset only) ·
  My memory · Projects · Organization (pending-proposals bar with inline
  approve/reject — the Phase 4 queue) · Entities; project/entity ref
  pickers from existing scope refs, ?tab/?ref deep links (contact card
  can link here); live-cache binding refreshes only while the editor is
  clean, dirty editors get a changed-underneath hint
- memory module gains a UI plugin (catalog-generated, @engenty/memory in
  apps/ui deps, en/de i18n); /mdl/engenty-copilot/memory redirects to
  /settings/memory?tab=profile and its settings row moves to Memory

Verified: 42 module tests (incl. tiptap round-trip + markdown-survival
under happy-dom), apps/ui + copilot suites green, ops contract exercised
live over HTTP (human-edit provenance, conflict 409, approve).

commits.message:
feat(remote): engenty-remote module + Mastra channels Slack runtime (Phase 1)

External messengers as remote chat interfaces to engenty.

- modules/engenty-remote: chat-tuned engenty.remote core agent (catalog
  meta-tools, brevity contract in AGENTS.md/SOUL.md), module_remote schema
  (bindings, identities, conversations, inbound dedup — used from Phase 2).
- apps/ai remote-channels runtime: persistent channel-bound Agent built from
  the module config, registered on the Mastra instance (initializes
  AgentChannels), webhook routes mounted on the Hono app. Every inbound
  platform event wraps Mastra's default handler in the engenty-tools ALS
  scope (service principal, single-tenant, approvalPolicy deny) — the same
  seam Phase 2's identity gate replaces.
- Opt-in via ENGENTY_REMOTE_CHANNELS_ENABLED + SLACK_BOT_TOKEN +
  SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET + ENGENTY_AI_SERVICE_JWT (env/spike credential mode;
  multi-tenant EngentyChannelProvider follows).
- Deps: @chat-adapter/slack 4.34.0; root pnpm override chat=4.34.0 so
  @mastra/core (chat ^4.29) and the adapter (exact 4.34) share one instance.
- Stayed on @mastra/core 1.49.0: 1.50/1.51 add nothing for channels but
  1.50 breaks heartbeats→schedules (trigger scheduler migration out of scope).
- Pro-only: modules/engenty-remote added to CLOSED_PREFIXES + snapshot
  EXCLUDES. Docs: docs/content/dev/remote-channels.md.

  approval cards). Telegram adapter env-gated (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN).

commits.message: pass SUPABASE_DB_URL + VAPID keys to engenty-ai
commits.body:
The AI service's env block never mapped SUPABASE_DB_URL, so in prod the
Mastra store (and thus the platform inbox + the web-push/email
notification pg pools) had no Postgres connection — the inbox fell back
to in-memory and the notification channels were inert. Map it through
(same ${..:-} pattern as the other Supabase vars), plus the web-push
VAPID keys (VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY / VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY / VAPID_SUBJECT; unset =
push channel off). Documented in deploy/.env.example. No image rebuild
needed — these are runtime env for the prebuilt engenty-ai image.

commits.body:
Realtime push on the platform inbox: every per-user inbox record fans
out to the user's web-push endpoints the moment it is emitted (team
records stay badge-only). Subscriptions live in ai.push_subscriptions
(service-role only; endpoint-unique upsert, 404/410 prunes) behind new
/ai/v1/notifications/push routes — config exposes the VAPID public key
(null = channel off; keys via `npx web-push generate-vapid-keys` into
VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY/VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY). The service worker displays the
payload and on click focuses an open tab (engenty:navigate message,
handled in AuthenticatedRoutes) or opens the route; enable/disable is a
per-device "Push notifications" section on Settings → Profile. The PWA
manifest + SW registration already existed, so iOS home-screen installs
get push too.

commits.message:
fix(team-chat): Slack bridge skips non-autonomous connections instead of erroring

The bridge runs autonomously (service principal), so the connections
policy denies every action when the connection's autonomous_mode is
"off" — which surfaced as a confusing "1 error" on sync. runInboundSync
now reads each bound connection's autonomous_mode up front and skips
"off" connections (new `skipped` counter in the sync summary + op
output), mirroring the inbox sync's autonomous_off handling. The
settings hint and the Connect Slack doc now state the setup explicitly:
set the connection to Autonomous mode "Full" and the write actions to
"Allow". Adds bridge.test.ts covering the skip vs. read paths.

commits.message:
feat(team-chat): email notifications via the tenant's connector (N4)

New email channel on the N1 inbox fan-out: a 60s scan in apps/ai picks
team-chat notifications still pending after a configurable delay
(default 5 min) and mails them to the recipient (core.users email)
through the tenant's own Gmail connection via the gmail_send_message
gateway op on the service JWT — per the decision to send through tenant
connectors, not a platform SMTP env. Policy applies: the connection
needs autonomous "Full" and send_message on "Allow". Without a Gmail
connection the run is a quiet no-op; send outcomes are terminal per
record (metadata.email_sent) so failures don't retry every minute, and
read-sync means anything read in time never emails. Kill-switch
ENGENTY_TEAM_CHAT_EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED, delay via
ENGENTY_TEAM_CHAT_EMAIL_DELAY_MINUTES.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: Slack bridge skips non-autonomous connections instead of erroring
commits.body:
The bridge runs autonomously (service principal), so the connections
policy denies every action when the connection's autonomous_mode is
"off" — which surfaced as a confusing "1 error" on sync. runInboundSync
now reads each bound connection's autonomous_mode up front and skips
"off" connections (new `skipped` counter in the sync summary + op
output), mirroring the inbox sync's autonomous_off handling. The
settings hint and the Connect Slack doc now state the setup explicitly:
set the connection to Autonomous mode "Full" and the write actions to
"Allow". Adds bridge.test.ts covering the skip vs. read paths.

feat(team-chat): Slack bridge (pro) — outbound replay, inbound sync, binding ops

New pro provider modules/team-chat/providers/slack-bridge (CLOSED prefix
in both publish scripts): mirrors bound conversations to a remote Slack
workspace through the connections Slack connector. Outbound rides the
module-bus message events with per-conversation ordering — post/update
replay with author prefix, markdown↔mrkdwn + mention-token mapping
(code-span safe, user_map with @Name fallback), slack ts recorded in
messages.external.slack; reaction-churn updates and deletes stay local.
Inbound is a pull sync per bound conversation over get_channel_history
(cursor in the binding, 5-min in-process interval + manual sync op),
importing through the open DAL as attributed bot posts so ts identity,
rollups and events match local messages. Loop guards: imported marker in
metadata (atomic at post) + known-slack-ts dedup. Management ops:
team_chat_slack_status/bind/unbind/bound_list/sync_run.

Open module changes (additive): PostMessageRecord.botId passthrough,
service posts allowed with botId, ./dal export subpath, Slack connector
mapMessage passes subtype through.

commits.message:
feat(team-chat): user notifications — mention/DM fan-out into the platform inbox (N1)

Posted messages (user and agent authored) enqueue one pgmq
team_chat_notification dispatch with targets computed module-side:
mentions and @here/@channel notify always, DM members by default,
thread participants on replies, notify_prefs.level="all" opts into
channel activity; muted and level="nothing" silence, authors and
agents are never targeted. The apps/ai consumer (kill-switch
ENGENTY_TEAM_CHAT_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED) writes one inbox record per
target onto the per-user partition inbox:{tenant}:{user} — the layer
the inbox module anticipated; the /ai/v1/notifications routes now
merge the team + user threads via the caller's scope. Read-sync:
conversations.mark enqueues a read dispatch that flips pending records
for now-read messages to seen. The desktop bridge renders team-chat
records natively (channel label + author + preview) from the
structured payload and polls with background refetch so a hidden/tray
window still notifies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(deps): pin @hookform/resolvers to the consumer's zod via packageExtensions

The resolver has no zod peer dependency, so its zod type imports resolved
through pnpm's hidden hoist fallback — and the team-chat dependency
additions flipped that hoist winner from zod 4 to zod 3, breaking the
zodResolver overloads in every form package. Declaring zod as an optional
peer makes pnpm link the resolver against each consumer's own zod,
independent of hoist order.

commits.message:
fix(desktop): resolve API/AI base URLs lazily + surface uncaught errors in the shell

The desktop shell installs runtime env overrides after the module graph
evaluates; the module-scope env snapshot in apps/ui config froze the empty
build-time values, so workspace/api calls went same-origin to
tauri://localhost, whose SPA fallback answered every path with index.html —
the context 'response' was an HTML string and the authenticated shell
crashed to a white window (resolvedAppearance.font on undefined).

Also add a desktop-only error overlay (window error + unhandledrejection)
so future shell crashes are diagnosable without devtools.

commits.message:
fix(a2ui): make show_ui actions + data-bindings resolve

Two independent defects broke every interactive A2UI surface (buttons,
row actions), while literal/objectRef surfaces kept rendering:

1. The root pnpm `"zod": "4.4.3"` override forced the whole @a2ui stack
   (and @engenty/a2ui-catalog) onto zod 4, but the A2UI binder introspects
   schemas via zod-3 internals (`_def.typeName`). Under zod 4 it recognizes
   nothing, so actions never become dispatch closures and `{path}` bindings
   never resolve. Scope the a2ui packages back to zod 3 via nested overrides.

2. The catalog now dispatches actions defensively (not relying on the binder
   resolving them), and must hand `dispatchAction` the whole
   `{ event: { name, context } }` payload — it reads `payload.event`. The
   handler had unwrapped one level too far, so the dispatch silently no-op'd.

Adds a binder-contract test asserting the schema still scrapes action→ACTION
and dynamic→DYNAMIC, so a future zod-version drift fails loudly. Verified
live: the show_ui "Details" button opens the offer in the pane.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
docs(wip): generative-ui — adjudicate the MCP-Apps-vs-A2UI challenge per use case

MCP Apps wins external widgets (shipped, ecosystem default) and arbitrary
generated one-offs (beyond-catalog expressiveness, sandbox stronger than
validation for generated code). It is structurally incapable of the primary
ask — composing our core UI elements with objects by reference — because an
iframe cannot host the app's React components, theme, query cache or
live-cache loop. Division of labor stands: A2UI leads internal composition,
MCP Apps keeps the external + arbitrary rails; internal MCP Apps widgets
noted as the knowing fallback if catalog+renderer proves heavy.

what it cannot do is share the app's runtime — copies and proxies only.

data plane without session/query-cache/realtime, theme re-push, border-bound
UI, sandbox protecting already-trusted code) and state G2's honest scope:
unbundled widgets, generated widgets, and module distribution.

commits.message: generative-ui — adjudicate the MCP-Apps-vs-A2UI challenge per use case
commits.body:
MCP Apps wins external widgets (shipped, ecosystem default) and arbitrary
generated one-offs (beyond-catalog expressiveness, sandbox stronger than
validation for generated code). It is structurally incapable of the primary
ask — composing our core UI elements with objects by reference — because an
iframe cannot host the app's React components, theme, query cache or
live-cache loop. Division of labor stands: A2UI leads internal composition,
MCP Apps keeps the external + arbitrary rails; internal MCP Apps widgets
noted as the knowing fallback if catalog+renderer proves heavy.

post) give every agent sanctioned channel access. Composer mention

fetch); agent messages render with an AGENT badge and a View-agent-run
link to the copilot thread. Kill-switch:

fix(team-chat): thread button opens a reply composer on reply-less messages

The message toolbar's 'reply in thread' button toggled a collapse set, but
the inline thread only rendered when reply_count > 0 — so on a message with
no replies yet (the common case for starting a thread) clicking it did
nothing visible. Track explicitly-opened roots in `openedThreads` and render
the inline thread when a root is opened OR has visible replies, so the button
always reveals a reply composer. Verified live: opening a reply-less message
shows the 'Antworten…' composer under the sky rail; toggling collapses it.

(per-server cache, 1MB cap, csp + structuredContent passthrough) and no
longer fabricates demo HTML when a tool declares no widget. The chat card
renders widgets through a postMessage JSON-RPC host frame (ui/initialize

authenticated per user and validated against the tenant's registered MCP
servers.

commits.message:
feat(objects): make object card actions follow the chat surface

Clicking a record meant different things depending on where the chat is, but
cards behaved identically everywhere: they always navigated, and always wrote
to the copilot pane store — even from the drawer, which mounts no pane.

Fill in the ObjectDisplayIntent seam (dead code until now) so the surface
decides:
- full-page chat owns a pane, so a row click opens the record beside the
  conversation, and a link that does leave for a module route hands the chat
  off to the drawer first (openCopilotShell, same entry point as the FAB) so
  it survives the jump
- drawer/floating chat provides nothing: the page behind it is the workspace,
  so rows navigate as any link would and the pane actions drop out

Also fixes the display hint, which never fired: it gated on having observed
its own 'running' state, but a tool part only enters the transcript once its
output is complete. Liveness now comes from the message, which does render
while the run streams (isLiveRun), keeping replay inert. Pane tabs get the
record's title instead of a raw uuid.

records it found and renders by reference.

feat(objects): make the whole card clickable

Rows already activated by surface (pane in full chat, navigate in the
drawer), but single cards did not — they carried a small inner 'Open' link
instead, which was also redundant with the pane's own 'Open full page'.

wrapper, and wrap the contacts and offers single cards in it. Clicking
anywhere on the card now opens it in the pane (full chat) or navigates (drawer),
matching the rows. The inner Open links are gone; in the pane the card gets no
href, so there is no nested anchor.

manager anchored to clients (org-contacts), scoped user/project/client/
tenant, with paid-services registry — the engenty port of engrdian's
vault, minus its flaws (see docs/wip/secrets-vault-module.md).

- Server-side AES-256-GCM with AAD binding ciphertext to row identity
  (anti-swap); ciphertext columns never granted to `authenticated`.
- resolve.ts: single authority for "can principal read secret X" —
  owner-scope membership (client access flows through project teams) +
  explicit/goal grants; agents never inherit scope.
- Agent reveal gated by createSecretsRevealPolicy (R10: agent identity
  lives only in the profile-policy layer, not the operation handler).
- Verified: SDK unit tests (crypto AAD + resolve truth table), live DB
  round-trip, and a full create->reveal driven through the app UI.

fix(secrets): enforce tenant boundary in secrets_list (BUG-1)

secrets_list queried via the service-role client (RLS bypassed) with no
tenant filter, so any authenticated user's list returned every tenant's
secret metadata (names/kind/owner — no ciphertext; reveal was already
tenant-safe). Add an explicit `.eq(tenant_id, ctx.auth.tenantId)`.

Found by the test plan's cross-tenant case; re-verified live: a
tenant-B user now lists 0 tenant-A rows, own-tenant list and reveal
unaffected. Adds docs/wip/secrets-vault-test-plan.md with full results.

after its 5min window, and turbo then tore down the whole dev stack.

commits.message:
feat(secrets): agent-gated reveals — identity forwarding, approval gate, durable goal grants

Close the silent-bypass hole where a copilot chat could decrypt any secret the
signed-in user could reveal, unaudited and unapproved, because agent identity
never reached core.

- Provision a core.agents security principal per AI agent: mapping column
  ai.engenty_ai_agents.core_agent_id (registry agents) + find-or-create by
  (tenant, name) for builtins, race-safe via unique index (migration
  20260719120000). ensureCoreAgentId is idempotent; verified against the local
  stack (apps/ai/scripts/verify-core-agent-link.ts).
- Forward x-engenty-agent-id / x-engenty-goal-id (goal = conversation thread)
  from every run context: conversation start/resume, generate path, delegated
  children (own identity, inherited goal), and voice.
- Widen PluginAuthContext with agentId/goalId; secrets_reveal now detects
  agent-ness from ctx.auth and audits the AGENT principal with the real
  goal_id (decrypt_for_agent) instead of mis-attributing to the user.
- Approving a gated reveal persists a durable goal-scoped grant: the approval
  artifact id carries {secret_id} (uuid only, never raw tool input); the
  approve hook and the voice execute path call the new module endpoint
  POST /api/secrets/:id/goal-grants, which enforces the approver's own reveal
  ceiling before upserting core.agent_goal_grants (agent_id null,
  capability secrets.read:<id>) — before the resume re-invokes core.

Verified against the live local stack: agent invoke 202 approval_required →
grant → 200 with correct audit row; wrong goal re-gates; non-owner approver
403 (no grant); plain user path unchanged. Chat-UX halves pending a valid
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY (docs/wip/secrets-agent-gate-test-plan.md).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
